knowledge.content: Santa Isabel College of Manila is a Catholic educational institution founded in 1632 and administered by the Daughters of Charity. It aims to form students who are academically competent, compassionate, and committed to service.
Santa Isabel College is located at 210 Taft Avenue, Ermita, Manila, Philippines near Rizal Park and other universities along Taft Avenue.

Santa Isabel College of Manila had its beginning as a charitable brotherhood when on April 06, 1594, “LA HERMANIDAD DE LA SANTA MISERICORDIA”, a beneficent institution dedicated to the care of hospital inmates as well as orphaned girls and destitute, was founded. It was governed by a committee called REAL CASA DE LA SANTA MISERICORDIA.
On September 1594, the committee decided to help Santa Potenciana College, founded in 1590 by Governor D. Gomez Perez Dasmariñas for the support of the orphaned daughters of his Majesty’s soldiers. From 1594 to 1632, more than 7,000 girls were reared and educated by this brotherhood.
Since most of the members of the Brotherhood were soldiers, liable to die at any moment, they planned to establish another College similar to Santa Potenciana in order to ensure the safety and education of their children.
 On October 24, 1632 - what was a beautiful dream became a reality, “COLEGIO DE SANTA ISABEL”, an undying monument of Christian Charity and Spanish altruism was born. Its first President was Don Juan Fernandez de Leon.
The school is administered by the Daughters of Charity of Saint Vincent de Paul.

Santa Isabel College of Manila is an empowering Christ-centered Vincentian learning institution. We commit to engaging the community of learners into becoming inner-directed, globally competent Vincentian leaders who journey with persons living in poverty situations and care for God's creation.

The Basic Education Department provides education from Kindergarten to Junior High School and prepares students for the Senior High School program.

The Elementary Department provides education from Kindergarten to Grade 6. The academic subjects are Christian Living, Filipino, Science, Mathematics, Englisg, Araling Panlipunan, Technology and Livelihood, and MAPED.

The Elementary Department provides education from Grade 7 to Grade 10. The academic subjects are Christian Living, Filipino, Science, Mathematics, Englisg, Araling Panlipunan, Technology and Livelihood, Computer Education and MAPED.
The Senior High School program follows the K to 12 curriculum and prepares students for college, employment, or entrepreneurship.
The Senior High School program offers academic strands including STEM, ABM, and HUMSS. The school also offers special programs such as Comnputer Programming, Music Program, and Culinary Arts
STEM stands for Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics. It focuses on science and math subjects and prepares students for careers in engineering, medicine, and technology.
ABM stands for Accountancy, Business, and Management. It focuses on business principles, entrepreneurship, accounting, and financial management.
HUMSS stands for Humanities and Social Sciences. It focuses on human behavior, culture, society, and communication.

Computer Programming is designed to equip the students with the needed competencies in designing, developing, and writing program codes using various procedural and object-oriented programming languages. This program also includes basic knowledge and skills in computer hardware, software, networking, and web design.

Music Program is designed to equip its learners with the skills and knowledge to appreciate and express themselves through music and appreciate music well above rudimentary levels. It aims to foster students’ interest in music as they are immersed in an enriched musical environment that includes singing, playing musical instruments, and composing. It strives to develop compassionate, creative, and well-rounded musicians.

Culinary Arts provides learners with the knowledge and experiences that will develop their skills as culinary practitioners, professional chef-like skills related to cooking activities, food preparation, and services as seen in commercial food service establishments. It is designed for individuals who aspire to pursue a career in the food industry.

The Higher Education Department is the launching pad for professional career. Rooted in our Vincentian tradition, we offer a dynamic blend of rigorous academics and character formation. Explore a diverse curriculum, in-demand programs, professional development and skills-based programs aligned with the Outcomes-based Education Curriculum.

Programs Offered:
- Bachelor of Arts in English
- Bachelor of Music (Offered Majors: Music Education, Performance, Composition, Liturgical Music)
- Bachelor of Science in Accountancy
- Bachelor of Secondary Education (Offered Majors: English and Values Education)
- Bachelor of Elementary Education
- Bachelor of Science in Business Administration (Offered Majors: Business Analytics, Marketing Management, Financial Management, and Human Resource and Development Management)
- Bachelor of Science in Hospitality Management
- Teacher Certificate Program
- Bachelor of Science in Information Technology
Students who graduate from the STEM strand often pursue careers in engineering, computer science, medicine, architecture, and research.
Students from the ABM strand often pursue careers in business management, accounting, marketing, finance, and entrepreneurship.
Students from the HUMSS strand often pursue careers in education, journalism, law, psychology, public administration, and social work.
Students who complete the Computer Programming program can pursue careers in software development, web development, app development, systems analysis, IT support, and cybersecurity.
Students who complete the Music Program can pursue careers in performing arts, music education, composition, conducting, sound engineering, music production, and entertainment industry roles.
Students who complete the Culinary Arts Program can pursue careers as professional chefs, pastry chefs, restaurant managers, catering entrepreneurs, food stylists, and culinary instructors.
Applicants must complete the online application form, upload their latest report card and 2x2 identification photo, and wait for confirmation from the admissions office.

Once admitted, prepare the original copy of Grade 10 Report Card (Form-138) and Good Moral Certificate, photocopy of recent PSA Birth Certificate, photocopy of baptismal certificate (if Roman Catholic).
Students must complete the enrollment form, submit required documents, and settle the necessary fees to confirm their enrollment.
Santa Isabel College offers scholarships and financial aid programs to help students access quality education through merit awards, need based grants, and external assistance.

The Senior High School Voucher Program (SHS-VP) is a government assistance given to qualified Grades Eleven (11) and Twelve (12) students officially enrolled in a private Senior High School. The voucher amount depends on the category of the student-applicant.

Eligibility:
1. Incoming students from public schools, ESC grantees, and Qualified Voucher Recipients (QVR) from private schools, and ALS A&E and PEPT passers.
2. Continuously enrolled in the succeeding school year.
3. Student did not transfer to Santa Isabel College after the thirty (30) day period of the school year as per DepEd SHS Voucher Guidelines.
4. Has not been retained in the same grade level at the end of the school year.

Requirements:
1. Photocopy of Form 138 (Report Card).
2. ESC Certificate from previous school or QVR Certificate issued by DepEd.

Privilege/Benefit:
 Government subsidy for a period of two (2) years of continuous enrollment from Grade 11 to Grade 12.

GASTPE-ESC (Education Service Contracting) is a government assistance given to qualified students officially enrolled in a private secondary education school based on the stipulated amount by the Department of Education.

Eligibility:
1. Incoming students of Grade Seven (7) from both public and private schools.
2. Has applied within the specified period.
3. Applicant must not be a recipient of another scholarship or discount simultaneously with an academic scholarship given by the school.

Requirements:
1. Accomplished GASTPE-ESC Application Form with 1x1 colored ID picture, white background.
2. Photocopy of Form 138 (Report Card) of the previous school year.
3. ESC Certificate from previous school (for transferees only).

Privilege/Benefit:
 Government subsidy for a period of four (4) years of continuous enrollment from Grade 7 to 10.

The Full Scholarship provides a 100% tuition discount for Senior High School students that is Rank 1 in their previous school.

Eligibility:
1. Isabelans officially enrolled in the previous school year and Incoming students of Grades One (1) to Twelve (12) (both public and private schools) Rank 1.
2. General Weighted Average grade of 90% and no grade below 85% in all subjects per quarter.
3. Grade level size is not less than 75.
4. Applicant must not be a recipient of another scholarship, or discount simultaneously with academic scholarship given by the school.
5. Has not committed any major offense stated in the Student Handbook under the supervision /authority of the Student Affairs Office/Coordinator. 

Requirements:
1. Accomplished BED Academic Scholarship Form with 2x2 colored ID picture, white background with full name.
2. Photocopy of Form 138 (Report Card).
3. Photocopy of Certificate of Good Moral Character.
4. Certificate of Ranking from the Principal as Top 1 in the grade level with school's dry seal enclosed in an envelope with signature across the flap. 

Privilege/Benefit:
 100% tuition fee discount for entire school year.

The Half Scholarship provides a 50% tuition discount for Senior High School students that is Rank 2 in their previous school.

Eligibility:
1. Isabelans officially enrolled in the previous school year and Incoming students of Grades One (1) to Twelve (12) (both public and private schools) Rank 2.
2. General Weighted Average grade of 90% and no grade below 85% in all subjects per quarter.
3. Grade level size is not less than 75.
4. Has applied within the specified period.
5. Applicant must not be a recipient of another scholarship, or discount simultaneously with academic scholarship given by the school.
6. Has not committed any major offense stated in the Student Handbook under the supervision /authority of the Student Affairs Office/Coordinator. 

Requirements:
1. Accomplished BED Academic Scholarship Form with 2x2 colored ID picture, white background with full name.
2. Photocopy of Form 138 (Report Card).
3. Photocopy of Certificate of Good Moral Character.
4. Certificate of Ranking from the Principal as Top 2 in the grade level with school’s dry seal enclosed in an envelope with signature across the flap.

Privilege/Benefit:
 50% tuition fee discount for entire school year.

The Entrance Scholarship is granted to incoming and transferee students.

Eligibility:
1. Incoming students of Grades One (1) to Twelve (12) (both public and private schools).
2. General Weighted Average grade of 90% and no grade below 85% in all subjects per quarter
3. Has applied within the specified period.
4. Applicant must not be a recipient of another scholarship, or discount simultaneously with academic scholarship given by the school.

Requirements:
1. Accomplished BED Academic Scholarship Form with 2x2 colored ID picture, white background with full name
2. Photocopy of Form 138 (Report Card)
3. Photocopy of Certificate of Good Moral Character.

Privilege/Benefit:
 Partial tuition fee (10%) discount for the entire school year.
The school provides modern facilities including air-conditioned classrooms, laboratories, libraries, and learning spaces.
Science laboratories allow students to conduct experiments and practical activities related to physics, chemistry, and biology.
Computer laboratories provide students with access to computers and technology for programming, research, and digital learning.

The school library provides books, journals, and digital resources that support students' academic learning and research.

Service Hours:
Monday to Friday (No noon break)
6:30am - 4:30pm
The school chapel is used for religious activities, prayer services, and spiritual formation of students.
The school canteen provides food and refreshments for students, faculty, and staff.

Students can join organizations and clubs that promote leadership, teamwork, and personal development.

Organization or Clubs inside Santa Isabel College of Manila:
1. Altar Servers - Assist the priest during Mass and other liturgical services, contributing to the smooth and reverent flow of the school's religious ceremonies.
2. Bible Club - A relaxed group for students to study, discuss, and reflect on the Holy Scriptures to deepen their understanding of their faith.
3. Vincentian Marian Youth (Children of Mary) - Encourages members to grow in holiness by imitating the Blessed Virgin Mary and serving the poor in the spirit of St. Vincent de Paul.
4. Liturgical Animators Club - Engages students who help organize & enhance the worship atmosphere of school masses & prayer services through music, and readings.
5. Louiseans - Promotes the values of St. Louise de Marillac, focusing on charity, compassion, and service to others, particularly the less fortunate, in a school context.
6. Society of St.Vincent De Paul - Performs works of charity and social justice by assisting the poor and marginalized in the local community with practical help and personal contact.
7. Book Lover's Club - A community for students who enjoy reading and discussing various genres of literature, promoting literacy and a lifelong love for books.
8. Computer Club - Focuses on developing skills in programming, robotics, and digital technology, exploring current trends in computing and competitive challenges.
The school clinic provides basic medical services and first aid to students and staff.
The school maintains security personnel and safety measures to ensure a safe campus environment.
Students are required to wear the prescribed school uniform during school days.
Students are expected to attend classes regularly and follow school attendance policies.
The grading system evaluates students based on academic performance, participation, and assessments.
Classes usually follow a daily schedule with designated periods for subjects and activities.
Students can ride LRT Line 1 and get off at United Nations Avenue Station. The campus is a short walk along Taft Avenue.
Students can take jeepneys that pass along Taft Avenue such as Baclaran-Dapitan routes and get off near the school.
Buses that travel along Taft Avenue stop near the intersection of Taft Avenue and T.M. Kalaw, which is near the campus.
Students coming from northern Metro Manila can take the LRT Line 1 southbound and get off at United Nations Avenue Station.
Students coming from southern areas like Pasay can take northbound buses or LRT Line 1 and get off at United Nations Avenue Station.
Nearby landmarks include Rizal Park, the National Museum, Adamson University, and the Technological University of the Philippines.
